_about: THE FOG-EDGE BOARD'S SCENE (builder BF, 2026-10-14, PROPOSED; a board rig, never a menu entry and never shipped: variants/ is excluded from the export). Seed 20261009, water on, FOG ON, two player units of one side: a light fighter (800 m sight circle, the circle-edge scenes) and a tank (600 m, the line-of-sight scenes in a valley). scripts/render/boards/fog_edge_board_shot.gd moves them to where each frame wants them (the other is parked in a far corner). Loaded by Sandbox.new('../../variants/fog-edge/scenario').

sides._about: Scenario side -> the World's side name (the interface's accent table in data/ui/ui.json knows allies and axis) and the callsign pool (data/names/callsigns.json). side_a is brick red, side_b slate blue (Alex). The players are side_a; the village and its defenders are side_b.

view._about: How the sandbox shows this scenario. Each can be flipped at run time from the knob panel (F2) or INKWOOD_<KEY> (scripts/debug/debug_settings.gd); these are the values the knobs call "data".

fog._reason: Board rig: the fog is what the board is about

plane_px._reason: Planes are drawn at their own scale, a light fighter about 36 px across at zoom 1 whatever the map scale (decision demo-baseline: planes_drawn_at_own_scale)

plane_min_px._reason: A light fighter never draws smaller than this on screen, so the planes stay findable when the view is zoomed out

start_zoom_max._reason: The opening view frames the players' planes, the first turn's carry-on flight and the village; it does not zoom in past this (the players are 2,000 m from the village, so the zoom is far lower than this anyway)

start_pad_m._reason: A margin round every plane and its carry-on end in the opening view, so none sits on the edge of the free area

start_look_ahead_turns._reason: The opening view frames this many turns of carry-on flight beyond each PLAYER plane (the enemy's plan is never framed: it would leak it)

start_frame_objective._reason: The opening view also frames the target ring and the village round it, so the first screen shows where the strike is going

track_sample_s._reason: Tracks (the flown path of each plane, drawn for the whole game) are sampled from each turn's history this often

track_line_px._reason: Track line width on screen; ink in the unit's side colour

bake_pause_overview._reason: The map view stops drawing new chunks once the topographic overview covers this much of the full render (see sandbox.json)

result_card_delay_s._reason: The result card appears this long after the playback of the deciding turn ends, so the last of the smoke and the ruin are seen before the card covers them
